The story effectively balances exteriority and interiority to create a realistic, emotionally flexible narrative. On the side of exteriority, the plot moves steadily forward through observable events, sensory details (the moldy books, the shrieking tools, the blue light through the plastic), and dry, realistic dialogue among the faculty and construction crew. This is seamlessly woven with Helen's interiority—her quiet reflections on institutional inertia, her grief over the ruined volume of Vieira, and her final, poignant meditation on time and permanence when she touches the newly installed membrane. Furthermore, the story captures a broad and believable spectrum of emotions across its cast, ranging from dry humor and bureaucratic frustration to anxiety, exhaustion, and a quiet, enduring awe.
